title: On the chromatic number and equilateral dimension of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the tropical norm
summary: We study the tropical chromatic number of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $χ_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, the minimal number of colors needed to color $\mathbb{R}^n$, so that no two points at tropical unit distance have the same color. It is the tropical analogue of the well-known Hadwiger-Nelson problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$. We have $\displaystyle \binom{n+1}{\lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor} \leq χ_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbb{R}^n) \leq 2^n$ for every $n$, where the lower bound comes from Sperner's antichain bound on a maximal equilateral set, as shown by Swanepoel.
